* {{usePipelineRun}} (replaced by {{usePipelineRunV2}})
* {{useTaskRun}} (replaced by {{useTaskRunV2}})

items.toString:
Create PoC of the software index in Backstage based on data in Pyxis. The PoC should validate during ingestion if the team members associated with the products still work in RH, and if not, send email or something, to show how we could use this mechanism to continuously validate data. The end result of the epic is working prototype and a video demonstration. Prototype will probably be thrown away after the PoC.

* Deploy instance of Backstage and write down how you did it.
* Create a entity provider that will create entities based on the product listings of RH products.
** [https://pyxis.engineering.redhat.com/docs/objects/ProductListing.html?tab=Fields|https://pyxis.engineering.redhat.com/docs/objects/ProductListing.html?tab=Fields] with vendor_label = redhat
** [https://backstage.io/docs/features/software-catalog/life-of-an-entity#ingestion|https://backstage.io/docs/features/software-catalog/life-of-an-entity#ingestion|smart-link] 
* Entity provider should also create users and teams that own said product listings
** [https://graphql.pyxis.engineering.redhat.com/docs/objects/TeamMember.html?tab=Fields|https://graphql.pyxis.engineering.redhat.com/docs/objects/TeamMember.html?tab=Fields]
* Processor should assign ownership of products to the appropriate teams and users.
** [https://backstage.io/docs/features/software-catalog/life-of-an-entity#processing|https://backstage.io/docs/features/software-catalog/life-of-an-entity#processing|smart-link] 
* Another process should check if the users are RH employees and if not, raise an error.
** [https://backstage.io/docs/features/software-catalog/life-of-an-entity#errors|https://backstage.io/docs/features/software-catalog/life-of-an-entity#errors|smart-link] 
** Information can be checked against LDAP (as Comet folks how it is done) or we can hard-code it for the demonstration purposes.
* Demonstration should show that we created entities based on data in Catalog/Pyxis and that we can query entities that are owned by people who no longer RH employees.

items.fromString:
The Conforma Results tab does not fetch all pages of TaskRuns from the Kubernetes API. The {{useApplicationConformaResults}} hook calls {{useTaskRunsV2}}, which only returns the first page of results from all three data sources:

* *Cluster* ({{useK8sWatchResource}} → {{K8sListResourceItems}}): makes a single HTTP request and ignores the {{continue}} token in the response.
* *Tekton Results* ({{useTRTaskRuns}}): uses {{useInfiniteQuery}} with cursor-based pagination, but only fetches on demand — the consumer never calls {{getNextPage}}.
* *KubeArchive* ({{useKubearchiveListResourceQuery}}): same pattern — supports {{continue}} tokens but relies on explicit {{getNextPage}} calls that never happen.

Applications with enough components/TaskRuns to exceed the default page limit will show incomplete Conforma results.

*How reproducible:* Always (when TaskRuns exceed the API page size)

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Open an application in Konflux that has enough components to produce TaskRuns beyond the K8s API default page limit
# Navigate to the Conforma Results tab
# Observe that only a subset of components show results

*Actual results:* Only results from the first page of TaskRuns are displayed. Components whose TaskRuns fall on subsequent pages show no Conforma data.

*Expected results:* All TaskRuns across all pages should be fetched and their Conforma results displayed for every component.

*Is this a customer issue:* No

*Please attach any logs/print screens to the ticket or share any additional info/links:*

* Affected file: {{src/components/Conforma/ConformaResultsTab/useApplicationConformaResults.ts}}
* Video recording attached (screen recording demonstrating the issue)

items.toString:
h3. Acceptance criteria

* When there is *at least one unresolved/active issue* with Critical or High priority associated with the current namespace, the *Issue dashboard navigation item* in the left menu of Konflux UI shows a *visual indicator* 
* When there are *no unresolved/active issues* for the current namespace, *no indicator* is shown on the Issue dashboard navigation item.
* The indicator *appearance reflects the highest-priority (or highest-severity) unresolved issue* for the namespace, following this logic:
** If any unresolved issue is *critical/blocker (or highest priority)* → indicator uses the *“error” style* (e.g. red, stronger emphasis).
** Else if any unresolved issue is *medium priority / warning-level severity* → indicator uses a *“warning” style* (e.g. amber/yellow).
* The indicator behavior and styling are *consistent with the UX/design guidelines* defined for epic *KFLUXUI-1228 – Visual indication of unresolved issues*.
* The implementation is covered by *unit tests* that verify:

Cicada should not update deployed_as field for existing product listings in Pyxis. We have ongoing discussion on this topic but while we don’t have an output is more prudent to keep things as it is.



[AC]

* Cicada shall not update deployed_as field for existing products.
* Cicada should allow already deployed product listings to set old value
items.toString:
Cicada rule to set deployed_as fied is outdated. Currently, it is the seting [“Operator”] when the product listing type is “operator controlled” and [] for anything else. The problem is the product listing type “operator controlled” is deprecated and no longer valid. According to Pyxis team, deployed_as field should be set as [“Operator”] if any of the repositories attached to product listing have build_categories set to [“Operator bundle”] and [] for any other case.



[AC]

* deployed_as field should be set as [“Operator”] in case any of the repositories attached have build_categories set to [“Operator bundle”]. In negative case, deployed_as field should be set as []
* Cicada should allow users to update deployed_as field, however should required approval from guardians in case deployed_as value is diferent from the one set automatically.

items.fromString:
h2. Context

{{formik-pf@0.0.1-alpha11}} imports {{Select}}, {{SelectVariant}}, and {{SelectOption}} from {{@patternfly/react-core/deprecated}}, which were removed in PF v6. We currently suppress these warnings in {{webpack.config.js}} as a workaround.

h2. Tasks

# Migrate {{formik-pf}} to PF v6 (PR to [patternfly-labs/formik-pf|https://github.com/patternfly-labs/formik-pf])

   - Rewrite {{SelectField}} to PF v6 composable Select API

   - Rewrite {{FormikWizard}} to PF v6 Wizard API

   - Bump {{@patternfly/react-core}} peer dep to {{^6.x}}

# Publish new {{formik-pf}} version to npm
# Update {{konflux-ui}} to use the new version
# Remove {{ignoreWarnings}} workaround from {{webpack.config.js}}"

<parameter name="additional_fields">{"parent": "KFLUXUI-1289"}
